summary.headline: Vardhman Q2 FY27: yarn business improved on demand and cotton-driven price hikes, while fabric remained weak with input costs up about 20% YoY.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as better than Q1 and the prior-year period, driven mainly by the yarn business, where demand from exports (including China-linked garment demand) and cotton-cost pass-through lifted yarn prices. Fabric was weaker: top line and bottom line fell versus both last year and Q1, hurt by lower export volumes amid US tariff uncertainty, domestic pricing pressure, and input costs up about 20% YoY. Management said order pipeline is improving, and it expects fabric utilisation and the synthetics business to improve in H2. Specific financial figures (revenue, EBITDA, PAT) were not read out on the call.

financial_highlights.metric: Fabric business top line and bottom line
financial_highlights.value: Lower than prior-year quarter and Q1 (no absolute figures stated)
About 7,000 shirts per day; top line about INR150 crores

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Improved on stronger export demand and cotton-cost pass-through; management said part of the gain came from trading gains on cotton bought at INR54,000-55,000 per candy, which may not recur. Spinning utilisation is near 100%.

segments.name: Fabric (naturals and processing)
segments.commentary: Weak in Q2: export volumes down on US tariff uncertainty, domestic price pressure, and new processing capacity underutilised. Utilisation was about 70-75% in Q2 and about 80% currently.

segments.name: Synthetics / performance fabrics
segments.commentary: Commissioned in March; still in sampling and stabilisation. Two customers approved and placing orders at about 35-40% utilisation; break-even expected at about 50%; management expects operating-positive in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Garmenting
segments.commentary: Around 7,000 shirts per day and about INR150 crores revenue; capacity being doubled at the existing location, with EBITDA targeted to rise from 7-8% to 13-14%.

guidance_outlook: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance revised to 16%-20% from the earlier 18%-22%, citing the cotton price rise from INR34,000-35,000 to about INR65,000 per candy.
Long-term revenue CAGR of 5%-8% considered a best case; 10-year historical growth about 6%-7%.
Fabric utilisation expected to rise from about 80% to 90%-95% over a few quarters; synthetics expected operating-positive in H2 FY27.
Announced capex of about 50 TPD open-end yarn project (about INR500 crores) expected to be operational in 6-7 months, adding about 8% organic capacity.
Renewable and biomass power savings of about INR1-1.5 per unit expected as remaining 50% of projects complete over next 3-4 months.
Madhya Pradesh PM MITRA Park land handover delayed 8-9 months; no new spinning capex approved yet.
capex_capacity: Open-end yarn project of about 50 TPD, expected operational in 6-7 months; about INR500 crores.
A 100,000-spindle new spinning plant estimated at INR1,000 crores or more (greenfield higher); 200,000 spindles about INR2,500 crores; build time 12-14 months. No decision taken.
Large land parcel at PM MITRA Park, Madhya Pradesh; handover delayed by 8-9 months; capex to be announced after Board approval.
Performance fabrics (synthetics) unit commissioned March 2026; utilisation about 35-40%, targeting 50% for break-even and near 100% in 6-8 months.
Garmenting capacity being doubled at existing site with automation; no decision on a second site.
demand_pricing: Yarn demand improved over the last six months on export demand; China garment demand has not declined and India supplies about 20-25 million kg per month to China.
India yarn exports about 110 million kg per month, of which 30-35% goes to Bangladesh; management sees no demand issue there despite wage unrest.
Fabric export volumes fell in Q2 on US tariff uncertainty; customer orders delayed by 1-2 months; management expects order pipeline to improve after recent US election results.
Cotton: New York futures about USD0.79-0.82 per lb; landed cost about INR64,000-65,000 per candy; CCI intervention unlikely this year unless futures fall.
Indian crop estimated at 28-29 million bales vs consumption of 35-36 million bales per Cotton Association of India survey (analyst cited); duty-free import window ends December 31.
Spinning conversion cost of USD0.80-0.90 per lb described as reasonable; yarn spread vs Q2 described as broadly unchanged.
Indian rated spindle capacity down from 52-53 million to about 40 million after 12-13 million spindles exited.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for yarn in FY28-29 and what is the ballpark cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Only one announced project (about 50 TPD open-end, about INR500 crores, operational in 6-7 months). A 100,000-spindle plant would cost at least INR1,000 crores; no new spinning capex approved yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for cotton prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Indian cotton tracks New York futures, which it sees at USD0.75-0.85 as a normal range; converted cost INR64,000-66,000 per candy. Analyst views on a tighter Indian crop suggest prices could stay firm unless duty-free imports arrive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bangladesh situation and how much yarn does Vardhman export there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wage unrest is cyclical and expected to settle around BDT17,000-18,000; India supplies about 30-35% of its yarn exports to Bangladesh and demand is unchanged. Vardhman-specific export figures were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fabric utilisation and peak revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Fabric utilisation about 70-75% in Q2 and about 80% now, rising to 90-95% over a few quarters. Management declined to give absolute revenue potential but said at least about 15%, and an analyst's 25% math was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A being considered to gain market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is open to deals but said smaller targets are in poor condition; organic growth remains preferred. It cited uncertainty over government cotton import policy as the main constraint on large spinning expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term growth, margin and ROE/ROCE expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance 16%-20%; revenue CAGR 5%-8%; ROCE to improve as debt-equity moves from near zero and capital is deployed. An analyst noted ROE has fallen from 15-20% to 11-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cotton yarn spread today compared with Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread broadly comparable to Q2 on current cotton and yarn prices; differences can arise from inventory cost mix.

qa_highlights.question: What margin benefit is expected from renewable power and modernisation?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40-50% of renewable projects complete; remaining 50% expected in 3-4 months. Expected saving of about INR1-1.5 per unit on power cost, with biomass boilers replacing coal.

risks_watch: Cotton policy: import duty-free window ends December 31; uncertainty over CCI intervention and MSP increases of 6-7% per year.
Fabric utilisation and synthetics break-even (about 50%) depend on order flow; technical textiles expected to incur small losses in year one.
US tariff uncertainty continuing to delay export orders and development cycles.
Trading gains on cotton inventory may not recur; yarn price sustainability depends on New York futures.
Madhya Pradesh land handover delayed 8-9 months, pushing back the next large spinning expansion.
Garmenting expansion and possible relocation depend on the business proving profitable.
summary.management_tone: Confident on yarn demand, pricing and the spinning industry's supply consolidation; cautious and somewhat defensive on fabric, attributing weakness to tariffs, capacity underutilisation and cost pass-through. Management was evasive on specific revenue and capacity-addition numbers and declined to commit on new capex or M&A until policy clarity on cotton imports.
